pillar_reactions.evidence: Rep tied it to surfing and joints — 'you're not just building strength, you're building conditioning and mobility at the same time... 30, 40 minutes, three, four times a week'. Prospect volunteered his own supporting case at length: 'surfing is really interesting. And that's the other thing I liked about kettlebells is that they combine both the metabolic... it was really exciting to be able to feel that full body kind of fatigue.'

Rep pre-emptively removed it as a need — 'in your case, actually, nutrition is already good, yeah, it's dialed in, pretty solid' — and gave the three-variable frame (what, when, how much, 8-10 hour window). Prospect did not push back or ask anything; he had already described tracking macros at ~130g protein.

Rep delivered it as the most important of the three — direct access to Trevor, his phone number, weekly check-ins, video form review, TrueCoach. Prospect's audio dropped mid-pillar ('I'm plugging my phone in. Can you hear me?') and when asked he said 'now I don't have any questions. That sounds pretty straightforward.' Understood and agreed, with no questions and no expressed enthusiasm.

anchors.raw: I did get Trevor's Guide, which is, for me, My level was basically what I'd already gotten from. It's very short. Like, that was designed more for somebody that was looking to start and jump into that.
anchors.note: The brand's own lead magnet is the anchor. He has already consumed the free product and judged it below his level, so the paid programme has to justify the entire gap from free to $4,000 with no intermediate reference point.

anchors.raw: I could spend a lot of time creating my own program, and then trying to optimize that, but one of the problems is that I don't really kind of, I don't know enough about kettlebells
anchors.note: He wrote a book on endurance training, has a physics degree and reads primary literature, and his son studies sports science and helps program for him. The real competitor is his own capability plus free content — his stated blocker is only kettlebell-specific knowledge, which is a narrow and cheap gap to close.

anchors.raw: you could do mobility drills and lift weights and all that kind of stuff, and, and it's just doing it consistently, not changing to the next thing, because the guy that's, that's pitching it, you know, looks better than the last guy
anchors.note: Delivered directly to the rep before the offer: he explicitly denies that the modality carries value and names the pitch pattern he is being subjected to. This dissolves the product differentiation the price rests on, and the rep did not reframe it.

anchors.raw: that's really looking at about 7,500 New Zealand dollars for me because of the exchange rate... that's a substantial portion of my annual income
anchors.note: USD pricing inflates roughly 1.9x into his home currency and he benchmarks it against annual income, not against coaching alternatives. A materially higher effective price for New Zealand prospects that nobody adjusted for.

anchors.raw: the $4,000 US dollars becomes about $2,800 US dollars if I run the business
anchors.note: The only supportive anchor on the call — a ~30% effective discount if his accountant allows it as professional development. It rests on a side-business intent he described as a maybe, and the rep did not help him build that justification.

unmet_demand.want: A short, finite engagement — enough coaching to learn safe kettlebell progression and then leave, not an ongoing relationship
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme is sold as 6 or 12 months. The rep met the want by improvising a three-month tier at $4,000 rather than by reframing the standard packages, so the demand was satisfied only by leaving the price book.

unmet_demand.want: Programming that works from a van on the road with two or three kettlebells and no gym
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep did assert the programme covers this — 'wherever you're going to be... you're going to pick up a kettlebell and know what to do' — but the prospect named this as 'the biggest thing for me' and it was never made concrete with load selection, kit list or a travel block. The capability probably exists; it was under-sold at the exact moment it mattered most.

unmet_demand.want: Programming and load guidance that accounts for two hip prostheses and arthritic shoulders
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep offered generic 'short mobility work specific to your needs' and claimed joint damage is 'impossible' with kettlebells, but nothing was said about how a coach handles a replaced hip, and no clinician input was proposed. Whether the programme can genuinely accommodate a prosthetic hip in loaded ballistic work is not established anywhere on this call.

unmet_demand.want: A route to coaching others — 'the possibility of doing something... to become a trainer' as a side business in his town
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme is one-to-one client coaching, not a certification or coach-development track. The rep acknowledged the ambition and even folded it into his summary ('maybe make a business out of it in the future') without saying whether the offer serves it.
